title: The map from the zig-zag module to the homology of the row-cokernel complex
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A=(A_{p,q},d,\delta)_{p,q\ge0}$ be a homological double complex of $R$-modules: $R$-modules $A_{p,q}$ ($p,q\ge0$) and $R$-linear maps $d_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p-1,q}$ ($p\ge1$) and $\delta_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p,q-1}$ ($q\ge1$) with $d_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=0$, $\delta_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}=0$ and $\delta_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}$ whenever defined; put $A_{p,q}=0$ if $p<0$ or $q<0$ and let $d_{0,q}$, $\delta_{p,0}$ and all maps out of or into a zero module be $0$. A morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ of such double complexes is a family of $R$-linear maps $\Phi_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to B_{p,q}$ with $\Phi d=d\Phi$ and $\Phi\delta=\delta\Phi$. Let $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q=\operatorname{Coker}(d_{1,q}:A_{1,q}\to A_{0,q})$ with projection $\pi_q:A_{0,q}\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q$ ($q\ge0$); since $\delta_{0,q}(\operatorname{im}d_{1,q})=d_{1,q-1}(\delta_{1,q}(A_{1,q}))\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{1,q-1}$, the map $\delta_{0,q}$ induces $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q:A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}$ with $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-1}\delta_{0,q}$ ($q\ge1$), and $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ is a chain complex of $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]; a morphism $\Phi$ induces the morphism of complexes $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$ with $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_q\Phi_{0,q}$. Let $Z_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A_{p,q}$ and $B_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)$ be the modules of zig-zags and of trivial zig-zags of total degree $n$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Then for every $n\ge0$: (a) for every $a\in Z_n(A)$ the element $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$ is a cycle of $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ (i.e. $n=0$ or $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(a_{0,n}))=0$); (b) for every $a\in Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A)$ the class of $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$ in $H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$ is zero. Hence $a\mapsto[\pi_n(a_{0,n})]$ induces an $R$-linear map $\rho^A_n:\mathbf H_n(A)\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$ on the zig-zag module $\mathbf H_n(A)=Z_n(A)/(Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A))$. (c) For every morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ of double complexes, $H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})\circ\rho^A_n=\rho^B_n\circ\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$, where $\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$ is the map of [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. No exactness of rows or columns is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing row-cokernel complex A.opcycles 0 and projection A.pOpcycles 0. HomologicalComplex.opcyclesIsCokernel identifies the latter as the cokernel of A.d 1 0. ShortComplex.exact_of_g_is_cokernel gives the corresponding exact short complex of chain complexes; map it through evaluation in degree q and use Exact.moduleCat_range_eq_ker to identify the horizontal image with the projection kernel. Evaluation preserves epimorphisms, and ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective gives surjectivity. The differential formula is the projection chain map's commutation equation. HomologicalComplex.p_opcyclesMap, evaluated in degree q, gives the morphism formula. These are the row-cokernel and induced-map constructions of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

source.place: Algebra, the paragraph before Lemma 00M1 (lines 18390-18394): 'it is clear that this induces morphisms of complexes $R(\Phi)$'; $R(A)_j=\operatorname{Coker}(A_{1,j}\to A_{0,j})$ is $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_j$ here

proof.text: For degree zero, the outgoing differential is zero by the shape. For degree n+1, evaluate a zigzag's defining relation at (0,n), using [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. It equates the horizontal image of the (1,n) component with the vertical image of the endpoint. The projection commutes with the vertical differential and kills the horizontal image by HomologicalComplex.d_pOpcycles, so the projected endpoint is a cycle. Compose the endpoint projection with the inclusion of zigzagCycles, and lift this linear morphism through HomologicalComplex.liftCycles. The kernel universal property supplies a linear lift, with its endpoint formula from liftCycles_i; this construction includes degree zero.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18449-18455: the canonical homomorphism $\mathbf H_i(A)\to H_i(R(A)_\bullet)$, zig-zag $\mapsto$ class of image of $a_{0,i}$ (the cycle property is not written in the source)

proof.text: By DirectSum.linearMap_ext, check the projected endpoint of zigzagBoundary on each direct-sum generator of degree n+1 [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. A generator in column zero gives the vertical differential, commuting with the cokernel projection. A generator in column one gives the horizontal differential, killed by d_pOpcycles, while its vertical contribution has endpoint zero. Every generator in a column at least two has endpoint zero for both contributions. Thus the projected endpoint of D b is the row-cokernel differential of the projected endpoint of b. If a zigzag a is in zigzagBoundaries, choose b with D b=a only within this proof. Every cycle c lifting its endpoint equals toCycles of that projected b, since iCycles is injective. HomologicalComplex.toCycles_comp_homologyπ makes its homology class zero [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18438-18450 (trivial zig-zags; 'we divide out by trivial zig-zags') and the converse direction used in lines 18484-18491 ('$a_{0,i}$ is in the image of $\delta\oplus d:A_{0,i+1}\oplus A_{1,i}\to A_{0,i}$'); the well-definedness itself is not written in the source

proof.text: Compose the linear lift from step 2 with homologyπ to obtain a linear map f on zigzagCycles. Step 3 shows that the comap of zigzagBoundaries along its inclusion is contained in ker f. Submodule.liftQ constructs rho on the quotient zigzagModule of [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. For any cycle c lifting the same endpoint, injectivity of iCycles identifies c with the constructed lift; liftQ's representative computation then gives rho([a])=homologyπ(c). No object is selected from an unproved existence statement.

proof.text: For a bicomplex morphism Phi, DirectSum.linearMap_ext proves that the endpoint of zigzagTotalMap Phi is Phi's (0,n) component applied to the endpoint. The existing zigzagTotalMap_preserves from [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module] provides the mapped zigzag b; unfold zigzagMap's Submodule.mapQ to compute it on representatives. HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap_i, p_opcyclesMap, and the endpoint identity show that cyclesMap of the row-cokernel morphism sends the constructed lift of a to the constructed lift of b, by injectivity of iCycles. HomologicalComplex.homologyπ_naturality [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] now proves the naturality equation on a representative. Surjectivity of mkQ and LinearMap.ext prove the equality of linear maps. No row or column exactness is assumed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_zigzagToRowCokernel {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) : let C := fun A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) => A.opcycles 0 let π := fun A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) => A.pOpcycles 0 let e := fun A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) => DirectSum.component R (ZigzagIndex n) (fun i : ZigzagIndex n => (A.X i.1.1).X i.1.2) ⟨(0, n), by simp⟩ ∃ ρ : ∀ A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ), zigzagModule A n →ₗ[R] (C A).homology n, (∀ A q, Function.Surjective ((π A).f q) ∧ LinearMap.ker ((π A).f q).hom = LinearMap.range ((A.d 1 0).f q).hom) ∧ (∀ A q, (A.X 0).d (q + 1) q ≫ (π A).f q = (π A).f (q + 1) ≫ (C A).d (q + 1) q) ∧ (∀ A B (Φ : A ⟶ B) q, (π A).f q ≫ (HomologicalComplex.opcyclesMap Φ 0).f q = (Φ.f 0).f q ≫ (π B).f q) ∧ (∀ A (a : zigzagCycles A n), (C A).d n (n - 1) ((π A).f n (e A a.val)) = 0 ∧ ∃ c : (C A).cycles n, (C A).iCycles n c = (π A).f n (e A a.val)) ∧ (∀ A (a : zigzagCycles A n), a.val ∈ zigzagBoundaries A n → ∀ c : (C A).cycles n, (C A).iCycles n c = (π A).f n (e A a.val) → (C A).homologyπ n c = 0) ∧ (∀ A (a : zigzagCycles A n) (c : (C A).cycles n), (C A).iCycles n c = (π A).f n (e A a.val) → ρ A (((zigzagBoundaries A n).comap (zigzagCycles A n).subtype).mkQ a) = (C A).homologyπ n c) ∧ (∀ A B (Φ : A ⟶ B), (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (HomologicalComplex.opcyclesMap Φ 0) n)).comp (ρ A) = (ρ B).comp (zigzagMap Φ n))
lean.note: The row-cokernel chain complex is the existing Mathlib HomologicalComplex.opcycles of the outer complex in degree zero. The existential natural family is uniquely specified on zig-zag representatives; no duplicate cokernel or homology notion is introduced.
